evaluator: stagebench blind evaluator (fresh agent, isolated workspace), with an independent review pass that re-measured every computed value and re-ran the judged probes
summary: Measured against build/ served locally, at 1440x900 in Chromium 158. Geometry is essentially exact: deck 0.5400, keybed 0.4600, width fraction 0.9400, aspect 3.0951, worst section-fraction deviation 1.2e-6; 73 keys (43/30) all inside the keybed, black-key height 0.610; all five reference colours within deltaE 1.7; 33/33 landmarks in their own band; 146/146 controls pass a 5x5 elementFromPoint hit-test; no forbidden rule fires. Behaviour matches: Organ, Piano and Synth are architecturally different (flat tonewheel sustain vs decaying FLAC samples vs modulated synthesis; six organ models spectrally distinct), every engine inherits the per-layer effects chain, Master Level 0 gives true silence, 36 voices render with zero clipped samples. Programs (32 + 8 Live), Store/Store As, splits, scenes, morphs, master clock, transpose and Panic all behave; a stored edit round-trips with zero mismatches and the dirty flag is truthful. The 11 spec-excluded controls move and do nothing else. One real defect: at 390x844 the panel is intact and 146/146 hit-testable at Fit, but every control is under 8 px and the zoom meant to fix that clips the stage to a 50 px band (0/146 reachable at 2x).

evidence: Envelope shape separates the three engines on the same note (C4, 1 s hold, captured off the live AudioWorklet output via a tee on AudioNode.connect): Piano decays 0.130 -> 0.000 over the hold; Organ holds flat at 0.057 for the whole hold; Synth is modulated (0.036, 0.023, 0.015, 0.041, 0.029). Harmonic-profile cosine piano/organ = 0.652.

Six organ models are each spectrally distinct, none a relabel: pairwise cosine over 20 harmonics ranges 0.518 (Pipe 2 vs B3 Bass) to 0.961 (B3 vs B3 Bass); B3 Bass is near-pure fundamental (h2/h1 = 0.010) while Vox carries a strong 4th (0.493) and Pipe 2 a strong 6th (0.406).

12 of the 14 synth waveforms were reached by walking the category/waveform encoders (Saw, Square, Pulse 33, Pulse 10, White Noise, Sync Saw, Sync Square, Multi Saw, Multi Saw 8ve, Super Saw, Super Square, FM 2-op A); zero pairs exceeded cosine 0.999, i.e. no two render identically.

Source kinds are different, not one engine with presets: the Program OLED reads 'RECORDED SAMPLES' for Piano A (Salamander Grand, decoded FLAC from build/samples/) and 'SYNTHESIZED PURE OSCILLATOR' for Synth A, matching IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json.

Every engine inherits the shared chain through its own FX-focus slot: with reverb switched on for the focused chain, the 1.2 s post-release tail measured 0.00962 (piano), 0.01134 (organ) and 0.00817 (synth) against 0.00000 with reverb off for each.

Routing is per-layer, not global, and behaves like the hardware: with FX Focus on Piano A the organ's tail stayed at 0.00056, and focusing the Organ chain exposed its own (reverb-off) settings at 0.00005.

All six units measurably change the rendered signal on one A/B: MOD1 rms 0.0526->0.0342, MOD2 0.0448, Amp/EQ 0.0675 with centroid 1.86->2.12, Delay adds a tail, Comp 0.0526->0.0704 with peak 0.355->0.523, Reverb tail 0.0156. The section ON switch restores dry output (rms 0.0516, tail 0.0000).

Nothing bypasses the master path and there is one context: Master Level at 0 gives rms 0.000000 / peak 0.000001 with keys sounding, and the connect() tee saw exactly one AudioContext and one AudioWorkletNode reaching destination (48 kHz).

Worst-case stress (Organ + Piano + Synth all on, all six effect units on for two chains, rotary on, 12 computer-keyboard notes held) reported 36 voices: rms 0.14723, peak 0.7664, 0 samples at or above 0.999, and the longest all-zero run mid-signal was 0 samples - no clipping and no dropout.
Cleanup is complete: voice count returns to 0 after release, and a window blur while a key is held drops 1 -> 0 voices.
Latency is playable: AudioContext.baseLatency 5.33 ms, outputLatency 16 ms at 48 kHz on the AudioWorklet backend (ScriptProcessor only as declared fallback).
Zero console errors and zero pageerrors across every probe session, including the stress run.

Lossless round-trip: 106 controls were driven on program 1.7, 87 of them changed state; after Store (two presses) and switching to another program and back, 0 of the 87 differed - a full-panel diff of data-step/data-value reported zero mismatches.

The dirty flag is truthful: the Program OLED gains 'E' and the accessible name gains 'edited, not stored' on the first edit, and both clear the moment Store confirms; an unsaved edit is discarded on program change (synth-on returned to Off after leaving and re-entering).
State survives a reload through localStorage key 'stage4.programs.v1' (5958 bytes): after p.reload() program 1.7 still read 'SYNTH A:PURE< B:OFF C:OFF / White Noise / wave 7/14'.

The only post-reload differences were Master Level (5.5 -> default 7) and which page the synth OLED was showing - global panel position and transient view state, neither of which the hardware stores in a program.

Pitch stick bends +/-2 semitones and is correctly gated per layer by PSTICK: with PSTICK on (Shift + Piano Layer B, OLED '> PITCH STICK ON') holding C4 and dragging right moved the spectral peak from 261.63 Hz to 293.66 Hz and left to 233.08 Hz; with the synth's PSTICK toggled off the same gesture produced no shift.

Sustain works from both bindings and reports honestly: holding Space (or clicking the pedal button, which relabels 'Sustain pedal: up' -> 'down') extended the release envelope to 0.004 at chunk 13 versus silence by chunk 4 unsustained.

Modulation wheel and Control Pedal both drive morphs: with Piano A Level morph-assigned to 0, wheel down gave rms 0.0737 and wheel up 0.0073, and the Control pedal slider gave 0.0763 at 0 and 0.00008 at 127.

Live Mode, Panic and octave shift behave: Live Mode shows 8 auto-storing slots, Shift+Transp cleared a held voice (1 -> 0) while the key was still down, and Piano Octave +1 moved C4's energy from 261.63 Hz (2.12e-2 -> 4.21e-5) up to 523.25 Hz.

Splits are editable and shown on the chassis: the split page exposes 3 points (Low/Mid/High = 4 zones) each with Off/xFade, the dial moved the Mid point C4 -> F5, and the deck lip carries exactly 11 split-point LEDs whose lit member followed (note 60 -> 77).

Zones route per section across engines: Shift + Organ Octave Shift reported '> ORGAN A KB ZONE 3-4' and the section's zone LEDs changed to 0110 while the synth kept its own assignment; with Organ, Piano and Synth all enabled a single key sounded all three (rms 0.10103).
Scenes switch layer enable without duplicating sound parameters: Organ On differed between Scene I (Off) and Scene II (On) and tracked the toggle in both directions.

Transpose and the master clock reach everything: Transpose +5 made C4 render as F4 (349.23 Hz at 2.09e-2, 261.63 Hz down to 3.09e-5), and the clock-locked arpeggiator ('SYNTH A ARP MASTER CLOCK ON (1/8T)') produced 11 onsets at 40 BPM versus 27 at 240 BPM over the same 3.6 s window.

Nine real drawbars (organ-drawbar-1..9, 16.52 x 67.73 design px, 4.1x taller than wide) each with an 8-step numbered LED ladder; pulling the 16' bar to 0 changed the 8th-harmonic ratio from 0.173 to 0.001 and rms 0.0483 -> 0.0355.
Six models reachable from the ORGAN MODEL switch (B3, Vox, Farf, Pipe 1, Pipe 2, B3 Bass) and all spectrally distinct (see distinctEngines); the LED matrix follows the selected model.

B3 percussion behaves like the original: switching organ-perc-on changed the attack (0.0330 -> 0.0274) and dropped the sustain level (0.0424 -> 0.0322), the authentic volume robbery, with Volume Soft / Decay Fast / Harmonic Third switches present.

Rotary is routed and speed-switched from the performance band: with ROTARY source on, amplitude-modulation zero-crossings over 2.1 s rose from 13 (Slow/Stop) to 25 (Fast), and Drive at maximum changed rms 0.0368 -> 0.0223 and peak 0.103 -> 0.071. Vibrato/Chorus offers all six C1-C3/V1-V3 types; its spectral sidebands move (0.287 off -> 0.321 at V3) but less emphatically than the other organ controls.

Three oscillator encoders drive a 14-waveform catalogue across 5 categories (Pure, Sync, Multi, Super, FM-H) with the Synth OLED reading 'WAVE n/14 / CATEGORY / IN CAT n/7'; 12 sampled waveforms were pairwise distinct (max cosine < 0.999).

Filter is fully live: Freq 0 -> 10 moved rms 0.0090 -> 0.0485 and the harmonic centroid 1.02 -> 7.42; the four filter types gave centroids 7.76 / 6.94 / 16.43 / 12.63; Resonance at max raised peak to 0.1901.

All three envelopes are present and read live values - the Synth OLED's AMP ENVELOPE page showed 'ATTACK 1.3 ms / DECAY Sustain / RELEASE 102 ms / VELOCITY 2' - alongside Filter Envelope + Env Amt and Osc Mod Envelope + Amount.

Voice modes (Poly / Mono / Legato), Glide, Unison 1-3, LFO (waveform, rate, mod amount, destination, Mst Clk) and the Arpeggiator all operate: with Arp Run on, the envelope showed a regular retrigger pattern (25 gate crossings versus 16 sustained) and the rate follows the master clock.

Seven layers across three engines each have On/Off, level fader with LED ladder, octave shift and KB Zone: organ A/B, piano A/B, synth A/B/C (organ-layer-a-level reported 'Organ A Level 70' on a keyboard nudge, likewise Layer A Level and Synth A Level).
Splits give up to 4 zones from 3 editable points with Off/+-6/+-12 crossfade columns on the split page, and section KB Zone assignment is independent per engine ('ORGAN A KB ZONE 3-4').
Scene I/II toggles only layer enable state - Organ On read Off in Scene I and On in Scene II while the sound parameters were untouched.

Morphs work from both required sources with a real indicator: after assigning Piano A Level, the control sprang back to its stored 100 % while the fader's LED ladder gained data-morphed="true", the wheel interpolated rms 0.0737 -> 0.0073, Shift+Wheel reported '> MORPH WHEEL CLEARED' and restored 0.0737, and the Control Pedal reproduced the same sweep.

32 slots in 4 pages of 8, reachable by the eight Program buttons, Page/Cat prev-next and the dial: headers walked 1.1 Grand Piano -> 1.8 Clock Arp -> 2.8 Gated Wobble -> 3.3, and Shift+dial opens the required numeric list view ('PROGRAM LIST 2/32' scrolling to '6/32').

Store is a two-press confirm ('> STORE TO 4.1: STORE CONFIRMS, SHIFT CANCELS'), and Store As opens a full character editor - 'STORE PROGRAM AS / Saw.Lead / DIAL: CHARACTER PAGE: CURSOR / PROGRAM 1: INS PROGRAM 2: DEL' - then a destination picker.

The 8 Live slots exist and auto-store: all eight read back distinct names (LIVE 1 Grand Piano .. LIVE 8 Clock Arp) and an edit made in a Live slot survived leaving and returning without any Store press.

Optional items are honestly declared rather than faked: Shift+Solo performs no undo, and IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json states 'Single-level undo for program change (Shift + Solo): not implemented, and nothing claims it' - matching the programs spec, which lists undo under optional. Excluded Pedal Tap answers '> PEDAL TAP IS NOT AVAILABLE'.

issues.title: Zooming at 390x844 clips the instrument to a 50 px band and makes the panel unreachable
issues.detail: At 390 width the stage container is 168 px tall at Fit and holds the whole instrument. One press of + adds '.stage--zoomed'; the instrument scales to 549.9 px wide (177.7 px tall) but the container's clientHeight drops to 50 px against a scrollHeight of 228 px, so all but a red sliver of the chassis is clipped. A 5x5 document.elementFromPoint hit-test over every control then resolves 3 of 146 at 1.5x and 0 of 146 at 2x, 3x and 4x (1466.4 px wide, scrollHeight ~500 px against the same 50 px window); the misses land on '.app--zoomed' and the status chips. Reproduced with and without mobile emulation. At 1440x900 the same control behaves correctly (clientHeight stays 606 px, 95/146 reachable with the rest reachable by horizontal scroll), so this is specific to the narrow viewport - and it is exactly the viewport where the zoom is the only way to operate controls that are 2.77 px tall.

issues.title: forbiddenDetection's displayElement rule is ambiguous for printed group legends
issues.detail: The spec defines a displayElement partly as an element rendering multi-character alphanumeric text on a dark fill, excluding a control's own printed legend. The panel's group-name chips (class 'lbl lbl--cut-dark', e.g. MOD 1, DELAY, COMP, REVERB, AMP SIM/EQ, TO ROTARY in the effects band and ORGAN MODEL, VIB/CHORUS, B3 PERCUSSION in the organ band) carry their own rgb(60,66,77) fill, so a hyper-literal reading would count 7 of them in the effects band and fire the forbidden 'OLED display' rule there. I scored forbiddenPresent = 0 because the reference photograph carries the same printed group names in the same notched rules, and the rule's own note states the effects band carries no display on the photograph - so the exclusion must cover printed legends generally, not only a control's own. Under the alternative reading the count would be 1 (effects). Performance, where the rule would also apply, has no such chip, so that band is 0 either way.

issues.title: data-section attribute collides between layout sections and the Program OLED
issues.detail: src/ui/Instrument.tsx:80 puts data-section={geometry.id} on each of the six layout <section> elements, while src/ui/Oleds.tsx:166 puts data-section={state.ui.section} on the Program OLED to record which engine the display is describing. Querying [data-section] therefore returns seven nodes at 1440x900 and element.closest('[data-section]') reports the Program OLED's section as 'piano' even though it renders at x 668.6-744.3, inside the program band (618.5-787.7). Purely a DOM-hygiene issue - no visual or behavioural effect - but it silently breaks any section-attribution tooling, including a naive landmark audit.

issues.title: Master Level and OLED page selection are not restored across a reload
issues.detail: After storing a program and reloading, 87 of the 87 edited program parameters came back, but perf-master-level returned to its default 7 from the stored 5.5 and the Synth OLED reverted from its AMP ENVELOPE page to the OSCILLATOR page (synth-amp-envelope data-step 1 -> 0). Master Level is a global panel position on the hardware and is correctly not part of a program, and the OLED page is view state, so neither is a round-trip loss of program data - but a player who sets a house volume will find it reset on the next visit.

issues.title: Default 390x844 fit puts every panel control far below a usable touch target
issues.detail: At the default Fit scale the instrument is 366.6 px wide, which makes a standard panel button 5.53 x 2.77 CSS px and a white key 8.02 px wide; the smaller dimension of all 146 controls is under 8 px (median 2.77 px). All 146 remain hit-testable and a touch tap on organ-on did toggle it, so nothing is unreachable - but the fine silkscreen is illegible and accurate aiming is impractical, and the -/Fit/+ zoom that would otherwise resolve it does not (see the stage-clipping issue).

evidence: At 1440x900 in build/ (served with strictPort on 4413), #instrument getBoundingClientRect = 1353.600 x 437.333 px at x=43.20, y=86.30. Deck [data-region="deck"] is 236.158 px tall and the keybed 201.175 px: deckFraction 0.539996, keybedFraction 0.460004, widthFraction 1353.600/1440 = 0.940000, aspectRatio 1353.600/437.333 = 3.095123.

The six section elements measure, in order, performance 0.1399992, organ 0.1999993, piano 0.0849988, program 0.1250000, synth 0.2500000, effects 0.1999994 against spec 0.14 / 0.20 / 0.085 / 0.125 / 0.25 / 0.20 - worst deviation 1.239e-6, and the fractions sum to 0.999997 so the chassis is continuous with no gap.

The instrument fits without vertical scroll at desktop (document.scrollHeight 900 = innerHeight 900) and the geometry is driven from the photo bounds in src/hardware/geometry.ts (DESIGN 9013 x 2912 design px, scaled by transform).

All 33 sectionLandmarks entries render inside their own band, confirmed from the DOM and from DPR-3 crops of each section: performance 5/5 (perf-master-level, the four-control Rotary Speaker block, perf-pitch-stick, perf-mod-wheel, and the 'nord stage 4 / HAMMER ACTION 73' wordmark at x=82.6 inside the band's 43.2-232.7 range); organ 4/4 (nine drawbars, red numbered drawbar ladders plus green level ladders, ORGAN MODEL switch matrix, B3 PERCUSSION Volume/Decay/Harmonic/On); piano 5/5; program 7/7 (program-oled at x 668.6-744.3 inside the 618.5-787.7 band, program-dial, program-1..8, Page/Cat, Live Mode + Layer Scene II, Store + Split, three Morph Assign buttons); synth 6/6; effects 6/6 (two bordered effect groups - MOD1/MOD2/AMP SIM-EQ and DELAY/COMP/REVERB - plus FX Focus Organ/Piano/Synth).

Reachability measured, not inferred: a 5x5 document.elementFromPoint grid over each control's bounding box at 1440x900 unscrolled resolved to the control or a descendant for 146 of 146 controls (0 unreachable); the same test passed 73/73 keybed keys, and it still passes 146/146 at 390x844.

forbiddenDetection applied rule by rule against the rendered DOM: performance has no dark plate at all (largest plate areaFrac 0.099 vs the 0.8 threshold) and no displayElement; organ's widest display candidate is 0.134 of the band (< 0.5) and 9 drawbar-like controls (4.1x taller than wide) defeat the 'generic equal-width control grid' rule; piano has only 2 tall controls (< 6) so no drawbar bank; program holds one displayElement at or above half the largest (program-oled, 2897 px^2, next candidate 162 px^2); synth's OLED is 0.23 of the band and no 8+ same-size controls form a regular grid (row pitches 45/39/3/24/3/3, per-row counts 2,1,1,1,1,1,3); effects carries 7 separating frame/rule plates and 12 distinct row pitches, so no single undifferentiated grid. Count 0.

Inventory totals: 146 controls (97 buttons, 26 knobs, 9 drawbars, 7 faders, 5 encoders, 1 pitch stick, 1 mod wheel), 242 LEDs and exactly 2 OLEDs (program, synth) - the only two primary displays the spec allows.
73 key buttons carry data-note 28..100 (E1-E7, the variant's documented E-to-E range); 43 have data-key-color="white" and 30 "black", and [data-region="keybed"] reports data-key-count="73".
Every key's border box lies inside the keybed rect (x 43.203-1396.803, y 322.455-523.628) with a 0.5 px tolerance: 73/73 inside, 0 outside.
Median white key 29.610 x 189.831 px and median black key 19.097 x 115.796 px, giving blackKeyHeightFraction 115.796/189.831 = 0.60999 (target 0.61) and a black/white width ratio of 0.645.
Pressed state is real: holding A/E/G on the computer keyboard put .key.is-down and aria-pressed="true" on C4, D#4 and G4 simultaneously, visible as depressed keys in the rendered panel.

The instrument was screenshotted at deviceScaleFactor 1 and cropped to its bounding box (1354 x 437 = 591,698 px); colours covering at least 0.05 % of that area were treated as surfaces (215 of them) and each reference colour compared by CIE76 deltaE to the nearest surface.

chassisMid #851a25 -> rgb(132,24,36) deltaE 0.52; chassisDark #5a0c13 -> rgb(92,16,22) deltaE 1.33; panelBlueGray #3c424d -> rgb(60,66,78) deltaE 0.65; keyBlack #0b0b0b -> rgb(10,10,10) deltaE 0.28; keyWhite #dcdcdc -> rgb(220,220,220) deltaE 0.00. All five are inside deltaE 12, so 5/5 matched.

The matched surfaces are the real ones, not stray antialiasing: keyBlack covers 6.65 % and keyWhite 2.74 % of the instrument, panelBlueGray 0.59 %, and the two chassis reds 0.10 % and 0.11 % within a graded brushed-red field.

Silkscreen is complete and matches the photograph's wording, not a paraphrase: 390 label elements including the top-rail jack legends (MONITOR IN, OUT 1-4, CONTROL PEDAL, ORGAN SWELL, SUSTAIN PEDAL, TRIPLE PEDAL, MIDI IN/OUT, ROTOR PEDAL, USB, FOOT SWITCH, AC IN, POWER ON/OFF), drawbar footages (16', 5 1/3', 8', 4', 2 2/3', 2', 1 3/5', 1 1/3', 1') and the right-edge service line 'HANDMADE IN SWEDEN BY CLAVIA DMI AB v2.0 Rev.B'.

LED hardware is differentiated rather than a single dot style: 242 LEDs in 7 variants - 133 red round, 41 green round, 26 yellow round, 18 left and 18 right arrow, 3 up and 3 down - which is how the drawbar value ladders, the model/type matrices and the split-point lip LEDs are each drawn.

Control caps are modelled: 31 knob caps with 26 pointer needles over 25 scale-mark arcs with 0-10 numerals, 7 fader caps in LED ladders, and 9 drawbars whose cap colours follow the reference sequence (brown, brown, white, white, black, white, black, black, white).

Two OLEDs with distinct treatments, both monospace pixel type on near-black (rgb(6,8,10)) in cyan rgb(164,217,238): the Program display has an inverted title bar, a 44 px model line and five data rows; the Synth display is a paged readout (OSCILLATOR / AMP ENVELOPE pages). Side-by-side DPR-3 crops against reference/nord-stage-4-73.jpg reproduce the VIB/CHORUS notch rule, the C2/V3/C3 arrow matrix and the MOD 1 A-WAH/WAH/PUMP boxes; the visible simplifications are that the plates lack the photograph's speckled texture, the knobs carry a tick ring the hardware does not, and the mod wheel renders as a bright chrome capsule where the hardware has a dark matte wheel - the first two are sub-pixel at the rendered 1440x900 size, the third is visible there, and none of them displaces or invents hardware.

Displays read live values, not static art: the Program OLED simultaneously showed '1.1 Grand Piano | E | SYNTH A:PURE< B:OFF C:OFF | Saw | SYNTHESIZED PURE OSCILLATOR | AUDIO READY VOICES 9 | MIDI OFF SUSTAIN UP | > SYNTH ON' - program number and name, dirty flag, layer summary, focused layer's model, source kind, a live voice counter, MIDI and sustain state, and the last action.

Control positions track their parameters and distinguish stored from sounding value: moving a drawbar updates its numbered ladder, and a morph assignment leaves the fader at its stored 100 % while the ladder gains class 'is-morphed' / data-morphed="true" and shows where the wheel has actually put the level.

LEDs follow the active layer and section: FX Focus reported Organ=On, Piano=Layer A, Synth=Layer B as focus moved; KB Zone assignment relit the organ's zone LEDs to 0110 while the synth kept its own; the split-point LEDs on the deck lip moved from note 60 to note 77 when the split point was changed; 44 LEDs were lit in the three-engine state.

Transient and page state is shown honestly: the Synth OLED switches to 'AMP ENVELOPE / ATTACK 1.3 ms / DECAY Sustain / RELEASE 102 ms / VELOCITY 2' when that page is selected, the Master Clock page reads the live tempo (120 -> 128 -> 158 BPM), and held keys render aria-pressed="true" with a visibly depressed cap.

At 390x844 the silhouette is preserved exactly, not reflowed: the instrument renders 366.600 x 118.444 px with widthFraction 0.940000, aspectRatio 3.095124 and deckFraction 0.539996 - the same proportions as desktop. Nothing collapses or clips in the default Fit view: all 73 keys and all 146 controls render inside the instrument bounds, document.scrollWidth 390 equals innerWidth, and the 5x5 elementFromPoint hit-test passes 146/146 controls and 73/73 keys.

It is playable but not operable at that size: a touchscreen tap on the 5.53 x 2.77 px organ-on button did toggle data-step 0 -> 1, and a tap on C4 (8.02 x 51.41 px) rendered sound - but the smaller dimension of every one of the 146 controls is under 8 px (median 2.77 px, largest 7.86 px) and the silkscreen is illegible at that scale.

The zoom affordance that would fix this is itself broken at narrow widths. Pressing + puts the stage in '.stage--zoomed' and scales the instrument to 1.5x/2x/3x/4x (366.6 -> 549.9 / 733.2 / 1099.8 / 1466.4 px), but the container's clientHeight collapses from 168 px at Fit to 50 px while its scrollHeight is 228 px at 1.5x and ~500 px at 4x: the instrument is letterboxed to a red sliver. The same 5x5 hit-test then resolves 3/146 controls at 1.5x and 0/146 at 2x, 3x and 4x, the misses landing on '.app--zoomed' and the status chips. Reproduced in both mobile-emulated and desktop-emulated contexts at 390 width; at 1440 width the same zoom keeps clientHeight 606 and 95/146 reachable, so the fault is specific to the narrow viewport.

Scored 3 rather than 4: the instrument is retained, recognizable and complete at 390x844, but the only path to operating the panel there regresses it - a simplification a player would notice immediately.
